Days 4-7 of Claude autonomously shipping to my SaaS:

Lots of improvements since my last update on Thursday:
- Previously, every hour, Claude would poke around the codebase, find something to improve, fix it, create a PR, merge it, run checks, and ship it to production. Having it ship to prod 24/7 was stressful though, so I updated it to create and merge PRs into a `dev` branch, and then every weekday at 9am while I'm around it runs through a checklist (security checks, etc), merges them all into master, deploys them to production, and then monitors server logs for 45 minutes to watch for issues.
- Similarly, exploring the codebase to identify issues every run is inefficient, so now it maintains a backlog and whenever that backlog is empty, it spends its run populating it, otherwise it picks items from the list to implement. And instead of just picking one item off the list, I'm now having it pick 2, so figure 23 runs/day * up to 2 PRs each = ~46 commits/day currently.
- Got the test suite down from 6-8 minutes per run to ~35 seconds thanks to repeatedly prompting Claude to make the tests run faster.
- Shortened its Slack messages so I'm more likely to read them
- Having it make endless backend and documentation improvements was getting boring, so I gave it a thumbs up to spend half of its runs on SEO improvements this week. Not programmatic SEO, but polishing the existing site. It has API access to Google Search Console, so can do things like this now (an example from overnight):

> /research was titled "Timeline Maker for Historical Research" while ranking position 8.8 for "academic timeline software" with zero clicks. Now "History Timeline Maker & Academic Timeline Software", an exact match for both its biggest non-brand query and its biggest zero-click one.

A good way to think about the current setup is that Fable is working 24/7 as a maintenance engineer (improving the quality of the codebase, one small change at a time), technical writer (improving the docs), and SEO strategist. Not bad for 1 week of experimenting with this.

Create a premium professional AI Image Prompt Formula Infographic based entirely on the user-provided reference image.
The provided image is the source of truth. First, carefully analyze the image and reverse-engineer its visual characteristics. Then create a polished educational infographic that explains exactly how this particular image can be recreated through an AI image-generation prompt.
This is NOT a character sheet.
This is NOT a generic prompt template.
This is a visual reverse-engineering prompt formula for the provided image.
1. ANALYZE THE PROVIDED IMAGE
Extract and describe the actual visual information visible in the reference image, including:
- Subject identity and appearance
- Gender and approximate age
- Face and facial features
- Hair style, length, color and texture
- Skin appearance and realistic details
- Body type and proportions
- Clothing and accessories
- Facial expression
- Pose and body language
- Hand and leg positioning
- Head direction and eye direction
- Subject orientation
- Environment and location
- Background elements
- Foreground elements
- Composition
- Framing
- Subject placement
- Perspective
- Camera viewpoint
- Shot type
- Camera distance
- Lens / focal-length look
- Depth of field
- Lighting source
- Lighting direction
- Lighting quality
- Shadow behavior
- Color temperature
- Color palette
- Overall photographic style
- Mood and atmosphere
- Material and fabric appearance
- Hair and skin realism
- Reflections and environmental details
- Any subtle visual details that contribute to the final appearance
Do NOT invent details that are not visually supported by the image. If a technical camera setting cannot be reliably inferred, provide a reasonable photographic approximation rather than pretending it is known.
2. CREATE THE INFOGRAPHIC
Place the provided human/image subject prominently in the center.
Around the subject, create clean professional information panels connected with thin lines.
Use these sections:
SUBJECT
Show the actual subject description extracted from the image.
POSE & BODY LANGUAGE
Show the exact visible pose, body orientation, hand position, head direction and expression.
SCENE / ENVIRONMENT
Describe the actual location, background and surrounding elements.
COMPOSITION
Explain the actual framing, subject placement, negative space and perspective.
CAMERA / SHOT
Describe the most likely shot type, viewpoint, camera distance and photographic perspective.
LIGHTING
Describe the visible light source, direction, softness, intensity, shadows and color temperature.
STYLE / MOOD
Describe the actual photographic aesthetic, mood and visual character.
CAMERA SETTINGS
Provide an estimated professional camera setup appropriate for reproducing the image:
lens / focal length, aperture, ISO, shutter speed and depth of field.
Clearly label these as recommended/estimated settings when they cannot be directly known from the image.
MATERIAL & REALISM
Describe visible skin texture, hair strands, fabric texture, reflections, shadows and natural imperfections needed to reproduce the realism.
DETAILS
Include important small visual elements that significantly affect the final result.
3. CREATE THE IMAGE-SPECIFIC PROMPT FORMULA
At the bottom, create a prominent box titled:
IMAGE → PROMPT FORMULA
Show the structure:
SUBJECT + POSE + SCENE + COMPOSITION + CAMERA + LIGHTING + STYLE + SETTINGS + REALISM + DETAILS
Then create another large box titled:
RECONSTRUCTED FULL PROMPT
Write one complete, professional AI image-generation prompt specifically reconstructed from the provided image.
The final prompt must combine ALL important visual information extracted from the image into one coherent natural-language prompt.
The reconstructed prompt should be detailed enough that another image-generation model could use it to recreate the visual as closely as possible.
4. IMPORTANT PRINCIPLE
The infographic must be image-specific.
If the user provides a completely different image — for example:
- a man in a street
- a woman in a studio
- a fashion editorial
- a cinematic portrait
- a travel photograph
- a product photograph
- a lifestyle scene
the system must analyze THAT image and generate a completely different formula based on its actual visual content.
Do not use the same example subject, clothing, pose, environment or lighting for every image.
The provided image determines the content of the formula.
5. VISUAL DESIGN
Create a premium editorial AI-education infographic.
Use:
- sophisticated off-white / neutral background
- elegant typography
- clean information hierarchy
- professional rounded cards
- thin connector lines
- subtle minimalist icons
- balanced spacing
- strong alignment
- generous whitespace
- restrained professional color accents
- magazine-quality information design
The central subject/image should remain visually dominant.
The information panels should be highly organized and easy to scan.
6. FINAL PURPOSE
The finished infographic should teach the viewer:
“Give AI any image → analyze its visual components → break them into structured prompt elements → combine those elements into one complete recreation prompt.”
The final output must therefore function as both:
1. A visual analysis of the provided image.
2. A complete, image-specific prompt formula that can be reused to recreate that image.
Do not make it a generic character sheet or generic AI prompting poster.
The user's uploaded image is the source of truth.

A 23-year-old built an AI character in 6 days using Claude, and cleared $14,200 in her second month.

He trained a custom LoRA on 85 renders, locked the seed, and kept natural skin texture with subtle body motion on purpose. Hyper-polished renders get flagged as AI slop. Micro-movements don't.

She posts 4 times a day on X and Instagram. Bedroom routines. Mirror loops. Outfit checks. Adjusting her hair in tight frames. Every crop is slightly off-center so image search never gets a clean match.

Replies land in under 28 seconds. An agent reads the comment, pulls the user from a 9,400-profile memory file, checks previous interactions, and chats like it actually remembers them.

Then he realized something: $41,000 in one month — one metric turned out to matter more than views.

At first, he judged content by pure reach and tried to make every frame look like a high-fashion editorial.

Then he noticed a massive disconnect: a post with 500k views made almost $0, while a 10-second casual loop brought in waves of paying subscribers.

He stopped tracking vanity reach and started feeding purchase data back into AI to find patterns that actually drive cash flow.

Watch how this 10-second loop is built:

0–3 sec: Close-up portrait as she adjusts her hair. The locked seed keeps natural fingers and facial geometry fixed.

3–6 sec: Full-body reveal in the floral playsuit — hands up to her head with zero skin distortion or mesh tearing.

6–10 sec: Smooth pivot with hands behind her back, seamlessly looping the video to force a 120%+ completion rate.

One generation sequence no longer ends with one post. He slices it into micro-content, tests performance metrics, and lets the software auto-suggest next week's baseline.

The persistent character pulled them in. The memory agent keeps them paying. ⚡

"On-Policy Self-Distillation in Diffusion Models"

Diffusion RL gets a reward only after the final image, even though the model actually acts through many intermediate denoising steps.

DiffusionOPSD turns that endpoint reward into explicit reward-improving targets at the model’s own intermediate states, then distills those targets back into the model and continually refreshes them on-policy.

Across two diffusion backbones and ten evaluators, it gets the best held-out score in 19 of 20 settings while cutting training GPU-hours by up to 63%.

The key idea is treating diffusion alignment less like noisy trajectory-level RL and more like continuously refreshed self-distillation with direct intermediate supervision.
